Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- Assessment consistent with urinary tract infection (cystitis): presenting with lower middle abdominal pain, pink (hematuric) urine, mild urinary frequency, nausea without vomiting, feeling hot/sweaty, and low-grade temperature (37°C measured once)  
- Past constipation may contribute to some abdominal discomfort but does not fully explain symptoms or hematuria  
- Pelvic inflammatory disease less likely given absence of vaginal discharge, abnormal bleeding, sexual history, or systemic infection signs but remains a medium likelihood diagnosis to consider in differential  
- Bladder or pelvic neoplasm unlikely given acute onset and lack of other systemic or chronic symptoms  
- No signs of severe infection (no back pain, no fever spikes, no systemic illness) at current assessment  
- Allergic history precludes use of amoxicillin

- Prescribed a three-day course of antibiotics for suspected urinary tract infection; specific antibiotic name/dose/route/frequency not documented  
- Advised to start antibiotics as soon as available  
- Recommended prompt return or follow-up if pain worsens, fever develops, back pain appears, new symptoms emerge, or if symptoms recur

- Constipation-related abdominal pain: Medium likelihood — recent constipation history may contribute but current normal bowel movements and hematuria not explained
